headline: Hark, a startup founded less than a year ago by Brett Adcock, released Hark Pro to everyone, an AI assistant that operates a person's computer for them.
score_reason: Real wide release of a new assistant, but TechCrunch notes claims are the company's and the product is unproven; score kept.
importance_line: People who want an assistant that does tasks on their computer get another option, but it needs access to email, calendar and cards, and the company's claims of working better than rivals are untested.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Hark, a startup founded by serial founder Brett Adcock less than a year ago, widely released Hark Pro on 6 Oct 2026, an assistant built on a model trained for computer use that carries out tasks on the user's own computer, free to start with a paid tier for heavy users and a hardware device promised for 2027. Hark says it will not sell ads or data, though users must connect their email, calendar and payment cards; yesterday we carried a headline saying Figure planned to release Hark this week, and today's news is that the wide release has happened.
notes: Follow-up of the 6 Oct pool item "Figure plans to release Hark AI assistant this week". The TechCrunch text does not mention Figure, so the link between Figure and Hark rests on yesterday's headline only.
